issues.title: Routines: run a saved prompt on a schedule, on this computer

labels.name: ci:e2e
labels.description: Run the full browser suite (Inbox window e2e) on this PR

issues.body:
Draft until the owner has approved the built screens and every string below. Not to be merged before that.

Head: `78a3d3718` (main merged in at `0c7d8fb72`; main has moved since, one more merge is due). Reviewed by the maintainer through `8461b5c39`. After that: row labels that name the routine, the owner's notes (the Run button beside the title in the narrow list, the editor's "Repo or folder" label, the phone folder picker fixed), and the rename to Routines.

## What it is

A routine is a saved prompt with a name, a schedule and a folder. When it is due, the Inbox on this computer starts a fresh agent session in that folder, and every run lands in one thread. It is a capability switch in Settings, off by default. While it is off nothing runs, no timer is set, no file is written and the sidebar row is not shown.

- **Schedules:** hourly, daily, weekdays, weekly, once, a custom cron, or none (run by hand). The next run shows as you edit. Scheduled times are at least 15 minutes apart; that is the only limit.
- **Missed runs:** one setting per routine, "Run once when I'm back" (default) or "Skip it". A catch-up is one run for the latest missed time, never a burst, and none when the next on-time run is under 15 minutes away. A due time while a run is still going is skipped.
- **A run** is its own launch inside the one thread (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi), with the person's own permission mode, in the folder as it is. A reply goes to the newest run's session. Ordinary launched threads keep exactly one launch; a test pins it.
- **Agents** use the `routine` tool action (and `plannotator routine <op>`). One an agent creates arrives off: the first turning-on is the person's. After that an agent may update, turn on or off, run and delete, and each change posts one line in its thread, showing old and new for the prompt, schedule, folder and agent. An agent's change of folder or agent turns it off again until the person turns it on.
- **Start at login:** while the switch is on, one login item starts the Inbox quietly (launchd on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux where available). Turning the switch off or `plannotator uninstall` removes it without stopping the running Inbox.
- **Not on Windows**, where the Inbox cannot start agents yet.

On screen and to agents this is **Routines** (the owner's pick). In code it is `scheduled`: internal names were kept. New code lives in new files (`packages/core/inbox-scheduled*.ts`, `packages/server/inbox-scheduled*.ts`, `packages/inbox/scheduled/`) with one-line hooks into the big files. No size ceiling was raised; four went down. One new dependency: `croner`, pinned.

## Proved by running it

A sandboxed Inbox (temp data dir and home, a stub agent, headless Chromium) driven through the real window against the real server:

1. Off is off: routes answer `routines_off`, no file, no login item. On: the row appears and the login item is written only under the sandbox.
2. Create and edit in the window; the next run follows the edit; a 5-minute custom schedule is refused in place and not saved.
3. A run at its time: the "Run 1" divider, the reply, the routine as the sender in the list.
4. A second run lands in the same thread; a reply reaches Run 2's session and Run 1's is not woken.
5. Run now pressed twice gives one run (one 202, one 409). Stop works.
6. A run that ends with no reply reads "Didn't finish", with the warn mark on the Inbox row only.
7. A late run after the server was suspended across a due time: one run, with its due and ran times. Several missed: still one, with the count.
8. "Skip it": a skip line, no run, and the earlier session is not woken.
9. Five restarts: nothing lost, nothing run twice.
10. An agent-made one arrives off; `on` and `run` are refused until the person turns it on; then a prompt edit posts a diff and a folder change turns it off.
11. Capability off: the row and the login item go, the Inbox stays up, nothing runs at the next due time.
12. The list, editor and thread at 390 and 768 wide, light and dark.
13. A first run that cannot start (the folder is gone) writes a visible "didn't start" line. A second Inbox cannot start on the same data dir.
14. With multi-select, row swipe and the Archived group (new on main): a routine's row picks and swipes like any row. Archived by bulk Archive, swipe or Combine, its schedule keeps running into the same thread, and a run's reply brings the thread back like any archived thread. Snoozed, it stays snoozed until its time. Combine does not move run dividers; later runs stay in the routine's own thread.
15. On a phone, picking a repo in the editor: a project, "Another folder…" and "New scratch folder" each save and show. (This was broken and is fixed: the picker opened below the screen.)

## Not proved

- A real launchd or systemd login item (tests inject the directory).
- A real agent CLI. Runs were proved with the launcher's stub agent.
- Two linked machines together. A reply from a linked machine is forwarded to the owning machine, where the same rule applies; that was read, not run.

## Known gaps in this version

- A routine is managed on the computer that made it. Its runs' thread works from a linked machine like any thread (see, reply, stop), and there its footer reads "Routine on <machine>. Manage it there." In a linked machine's Inbox list, such a thread is an ordinary row (no play mark, no "Run 9").
- No event triggers (pull requests, webhooks), no cloud, no sync of schedules between computers.
- A cloud agent through the agent door is not offered the tool, whatever the switch.

## Changes from the written spec

- An agent's `run` posts one line in its thread (the spec said it posts nothing).
- An agent-made routine arrives off, and an agent's change of folder or agent turns it off again (the spec had agent-made ones arrive on).
- A catch-up counts earlier missed times up to 1,000 for its wording only ("Skipped 1,000 or more times"). Nobody can hit or set it.

## For the owner's word-for-word approval

The owner approved the agent text as first written. The rename and three clarifications changed only the lines in the first fold.

# Routines: every agent-facing string, verbatim (2026-11-15)

For the owner's word-for-word approval. Branch `feat/scheduled-threads`. Each block is exactly what an agent reads; `<…>` marks a value filled in. Nothing here is served while the switch is off except the off answer.

## 1. The tool `routine` (MCP, and `plannotator_inbox` action `routine`)

Title: `Make or change a routine`

Description (`packages/server/inbox-mcp-scheduled.ts`, `SCHEDULED_THREAD_DESCRIPTION`):

```text
Routines in the Plannotator Inbox: a saved prompt an agent on this computer runs on a schedule, every run replying in the routine's own Inbox thread. Make one only when the person asks for work to run on its own, on a schedule. op: create, list, get, update, on, off, run, delete; update changes only the fields you pass. One you create arrives off: the person turns it on the first time, in the Inbox; after that you may update, turn it on or off, run and delete it. Changing its folder or its agent turns it off again until the person turns it back on. A schedule's runs are at least 15 minutes apart. Pass thread_id, the thread you work in: each change posts one line there for the person; runs never reply there.
```

Field descriptions, in schema order (`op` has none: its enum is create, list, get, update, on, off, run, delete; `model` and `effort` have none; `project_path` is the shared `PROJECT_PATH_DESCRIPTION`):

- `id`: The routine (sch_…); not for create or list.
- `name`: A few words the person knows it by, e.g. "Morning triage".
- `prompt`: What each run is asked, in the person's words, whole.
- `schedule`: { cron: "0 9 * * 1-5", tz: "America/New_York" } (5-field cron), { at: "2026-11-20T17:00" } for once, or null: it runs only when run. tz optional: this computer's zone.
- `if_missed`: A run missed while the computer slept: run it once when it wakes (default), or skip it.
- `folder`: Where runs work: { path }, that folder itself (default: your project_path; never home, / or a hidden folder), or { scratch: true } for a new folder.
- `agent`: claude-code, codex, opencode or pi. Default: your own host.
- `attachments`: Full paths of files each run gets.
- `thread_id`: The thread you are working in: your change lines go there, not the runs.
- `agent_session`: Your session id; the `plannotator inbox mcp` shim fills it.
- `agent_name`: How the person sees you, e.g. "Claude Code".
- `agent_host`: Your agent host, e.g. claude-code, codex, cursor.

## 2. The off answer (a call while the switch is off)

```text
routines_off: Routines are off on this computer, so nothing was written. The person turns them on in Settings, Capabilities.
```

A cloud agent through the agent door is never offered the tool, whatever the switch: its call answers the door's own `tool_not_allowed: routine is not an Inbox action. Actions: <the door's actions>.` It never reads the off answer.

## 3. `plannotator inbox --help`, the tool's section (shown only while the switch is on)

Arguments: `op`, `id`, `name`, `prompt`, `schedule`, `if_missed`, `folder`, `agent`, `model`, `effort`, `attachments`, `thread_id`, `project_path`, `agent_session`, `agent_name`, `agent_host`.

```text
A routine in the Plannotator Inbox: a saved prompt that an agent on this computer runs on a schedule; every run replies in the routine's own Inbox thread, made at its first run, and the person replies there to that run. Make one only when the person asks for work to run on its own, on a schedule ("every weekday at 9, triage new issues").
- `op`: `create`, `list`, `get`, `update`, `on`, `off`, `run` or `delete`. Every op but create and list takes `id` (`sch_…`). `update` changes only the fields you pass.
- create: `name` (a few words), `prompt` (what each run is asked, whole), `schedule`, and optionally `if_missed`, `folder` (`{ "path": … }`, run in that folder itself, never home, `/` or a hidden folder; default: your project folder; `{ "scratch": true }` for a new one), `agent` (`claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode` or `pi`; default your own), `model`, `effort`, `attachments` (full paths). `schedule`: `{ "cron": "0 9 * * 1-5", "tz": "America/New_York" }` (5-field cron), `{ "at": "2026-11-20T17:00" }` for once, or `null` (it runs only when someone runs it); `tz` is optional: this computer's zone. A schedule's runs are at least 15 minutes apart; a closer schedule is refused with `schedule_too_frequent`. `if_missed`: `run_once` (default: one run when the computer wakes) or `skip`.
- One you create arrives off. The person turns it on the first time, in the Inbox; before that, `on` and `run` answer `routine_not_approved` and change nothing. After that you may `update`, turn it `on` or `off`, `run` it and `delete` it. Changing its folder or its agent turns it off again until the person turns it back on.
- Pass `thread_id`, the thread you are working in: every change posts one line there for the person, with a link to the routine and, for an edit, what it was and what it is now. Runs never reply there.
- Each run starts the agent the way New message in the Inbox does, in the person's own permission mode. Starting agents from the Inbox must be on (Settings → Agents).
- The person turns routines on and off (Settings → Capabilities in the Inbox). Off, the Inbox lists no `routine`, and a call answers `routines_off` and writes nothing.
```

## 3a. `plannotator routine <op> ['<json>']` (the shell form of `plannotator inbox call routine`)

Its own words, only on a bad command line (everything else is `inbox call`'s):

```text

invalid_json: The arguments are not JSON: <parser's message>
invalid_json: The arguments must be one JSON object.
```

## 4. Lines posted in the agent's calling thread (as the agent, with `scheduled_change`)

```text
Made the routine [<name>](#routine=<id>). It is off until you turn it on.
```

~~~text
Changed the routine [<name>](#routine=<id>).

It now runs <schedule in words> (was <old schedule in words>).

It now works in <folder> (was <old folder>).

It now uses <agent name> (was <old agent name>).

Its name was <old name>.

Also changed: <if missed, model, effort, attachments>.

The prompt:

```diff
- <each old prompt line>
+ <each new prompt line>
```

It is off until you turn it on again.
~~~

Only the paragraphs for what changed appear, in this order. The last one appears only when an agent changed the folder or the agent of one that was on or that the person had turned on. Agent names: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi. Schedule words (the row's words with the first letter lowered): "every 15 minutes", "every hour at :15", "every 2 hours, at minute 0", "every day at 9:00 AM", "every weekday at 9:00 AM", "every weekend day at 9:00 AM", "every week on Friday at 5:00 PM", "every Monday and Wednesday at 9:00 AM", "every month on day 1 at 9:00 AM", "once on Fri, Nov 20 at 5:00 PM", "on the schedule <cron>" for any other cron, or "only when someone runs it". A scratch folder reads "a new scratch folder", a removed project "a folder that is gone".

```text
Turned the routine [<name>](#routine=<id>) on.
Turned the routine [<name>](#routine=<id>) off.
Started run <n> of the routine [<name>](#routine=<id>).
Run <n> of the routine [<name>](#routine=<id>) didn't start. Its thread says why.
Deleted the routine <name>. Its thread and past runs stay.
```

## 5. Tool results (text the calling agent gets)

One line per routine (list, and inside the others):

```text
<id> "<name>": <on|off|running|done>, <Schedule words> (<EST>), <agent> in <folder>, next <ISO time>, not yet turned on by the person, thread <thread id>.
```

(`(<zone>)`, `next …`, `not yet turned on by the person` and `thread …` appear only when they apply. With no schedule, `<Schedule words> (<EST>)` reads `runs only when run`.) `<agent>` is the agent id (`claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `pi`). `<Schedule words>` is capitalized ("Every weekday at 9:00 AM", "Once on Fri, Nov 20 at 5:00 PM") and reads "Runs when you run it." with no schedule. `<folder>` is the folder as `~/…`, "New scratch folder" before a scratch one's first run, or "A folder that is gone". The structured result carries the whole row (`InboxScheduledRow`), which includes `thread_name`: the name of the thread its runs land in, or null before its first run. Then, per op:

```text
No routines.
Made <line> It is off until the person turns it on in the Inbox. The person sees it in thread <thread id>.
Changed <line> The person sees it in thread <thread id>.
Nothing changed in <line>
<line> The person sees it in thread <thread id>.            (on, off)
Started run <n> of <line> The person sees it in thread <thread id>.
Run <n> did not start: <the launch's reason, without "Nothing was sent."> <line>
Deleted <id>. Its thread and past runs stay. The person sees it in thread <thread id>.
```

`get` adds `Prompt: "<prompt as JSON>"` and one line per run, newest first, at most 20: `Run <n>: <started ISO>, <replied|didn't finish|running|didn't start>, late (<divider message id>).` (`, late` only for a late run).

## 6. Refusals an agent can get (`<code>: <message>`)

```text
routines_off: Routines are off on this computer, so nothing was written. The person turns them on in Settings, Capabilities.
routine_not_approved: The person turns <name> on the first time, in the Inbox. Nothing was changed.
routine_not_approved: The person turns <name> on the first time, in the Inbox. Nothing was run.
schedule_too_frequent: Scheduled times are at least 15 minutes apart. This one runs every <n> minutes.
schedule_too_frequent: Scheduled times are at least 15 minutes apart. This one runs every minute.
schedule_too_frequent: Scheduled times are at least 15 minutes apart. This one can run <n> minutes apart.
schedule_too_frequent: Scheduled times are at least 15 minutes apart. This one can run 1 minute apart.
schedule_invalid: That isn't a schedule Plannotator can read. A schedule is a 5-field cron, such as 0 9 * * 1-5.
schedule_invalid: That isn't a schedule Plannotator can read. <zone> isn't a time zone it knows; use one such as America/New_York.
schedule_invalid: That isn't a schedule: a one-time schedule is a date and time, 2026-11-20T17:00.
schedule_invalid: That isn't a schedule: <YYYY-MM-DD> at <HH:MM> is not a real date and time.
schedule_invalid: That time has already passed.
schedule_invalid: That schedule never runs: no day matches it.
routine_running: <name> is running now.
routine_not_found: No routine <id>.
launch_off: Starting agents from the Inbox is off. Turn it on in Settings → Agents.
folder_missing: No project <project id>.
folder_missing: <path> isn't there.
folder_unavailable: <drive> isn't responding.
validation_error: Pick a folder inside the home folder.
validation_error: Pick a folder inside <folder>.
validation_error: Hidden folders can't be picked.
validation_error: System folders can't be picked.
validation_error: Pick a folder by its full path.
validation_error: id: required for <op>.
validation_error: <name|prompt>: required.
validation_error: <name|prompt>: at most <80|100000> characters.
validation_error: schedule: { cron } or { at }, each with an optional tz, or null.
validation_error: folder: { path } or { scratch: true }, or pass project_path.
validation_error: if_missed: run_once or skip.
validation_error: agent: claude-code, codex, opencode or pi.
validation_error: <model|effort>: a model or effort name.
validation_error: attachments: a list of full file paths.
```

"runs every" is for a schedule whose runs are evenly spaced; "can run … apart" is for uneven gaps (`*/14` runs at :56 and then :00, so it reads "This one can run 4 minutes apart."). The refusal also carries `every_minutes: <n>`. "That time has already passed." is only for a new or changed one-time time; one saved before its time keeps it.

## 6a. Why a run didn't start (the reason after "The run didn't start." in the thread, and after "did not start:" in a run result)

The launch's own refusal, with New message's trailing " Nothing was sent." removed. The usual ones:

```text
Starting agents from the Inbox is off. Turn it on in Settings → Agents.
<agent> can't be started here.
<path> isn't there. Pick another folder.
<folder> isn't there any more. Pick another project.
<drive> isn't responding.
<folder> is taken. Pick another folder.
Can't open <folder>: no permission.
Hidden folders can't be picked.
System folders can't be picked.
Pick a folder inside the home folder.
Pick a folder inside <folder>.
```

## 7. What a run's agent reads

The run's first turn is the prompt exactly as saved. A late run adds, after a blank line:

```text
This run was due Mon 9:00 AM and started Mon 11:14 AM.
```

Both times are in the schedule's own zone. Run now is never late. Each run's divider also carries the saved files (`attachments`); a file that cannot be read is left out without a line.

## 8. Skip lines in the run thread (notes delivered to no session; an agent reads them only in read_thread)

```text
Skipped Mon 9:00 AM · this computer was asleep
Skipped 5 times, Mon 9:00 AM to Mon 1:00 PM · the Inbox wasn't running
Skipped 1,000 or more times, Mon 9:00 AM to Tue 9:00 AM · the Inbox wasn't running
Skipped Mon 9:00 AM · the last run was still going
Skipped Mon 9:00 AM · the next run was less than 15 minutes away
Skipped Mon 9:00 AM · it couldn't start on time
```

The last two: a late run that would come under 15 minutes before the next one, and (with `if_missed: skip`) a run the Inbox, up and awake, could not start on time. Times are in the schedule's zone; a count over one reads "<n> times, <first> to <last>". Turning routines on, or turning "Start agents" back on, starts from now: nothing that came due while either was off is run or written as a skip line.

## 9. Window-facing text the agent never reads (listed for completeness)

```text
Run <n> has ended, so your reply was not sent. Reply to the latest run (Run <m>) instead.
Routines are off on this computer. Turn them on in Settings, Capabilities.
Routines are not offered on this computer.
Routines aren't available on Windows.
A routine is changed in the Inbox window; an agent uses the routine tool.
scheduled_threads: { on: boolean }.
config.json could not be saved; nothing changed. A config.json that is not valid JSON is never written over: fix or remove it.
```

</details>

<details><summary>Every new on-screen string</summary>

# Routines: every new on-screen string

2026-11-15. Branch `feat/scheduled-threads`. Read from the code in the `sched` worktree. Each string is exact. `<…>` marks a value filled in. "aria" marks words read aloud only. Paths are under `packages/inbox/` unless named.

## 1. Sidebar

Source: `scheduled/ScheduledNav.tsx`, `components/Sidebar.tsx`.

- Row under Board, only while the switch is on: `Routines`

## 2. Settings → Capabilities row

Source: `scheduled/SettingsRow.tsx`. The row comes after Checklist. It is absent on Windows.

- Label: `Routines`
- Description: `Runs saved prompts on a schedule, on this computer, while the Inbox is running.`
- Added while on, where the Inbox cannot start itself at login: ` It does not start the Inbox when you log in on this computer.`
- Errors from the switch (shown the way other Settings errors are): `Routines are not offered on this computer.`, `config.json could not be saved; nothing changed. A config.json that is not valid JSON is never written over: fix or remove it.`

## 3. The Routines page

Source: `scheduled/ScheduledPage.tsx`.

- Heading: `Routines`
- Button: `New routine` (on a phone: `New`). aria: `New routine`
- While the settings load: nothing under the heading, and no New button.
- On Windows (no row in Settings): `Routines aren't available on Windows.`
- Switch off: `Routines are off on this computer.` then the link `Turn them on in Settings`
- Start agents off: `Starting agents is off, so nothing runs.` then the link `Turn it on in Settings`
- Empty: `No routines yet.`
- An action that failed: the server's message, as an error line (see section 9). A delete that failed: `<name> was not deleted. <the server's message>`
- aria for the page region: `Routines`

## 4. The list (table)

Source: `scheduled/ScheduledTable.tsx`, `scheduled/words.ts`.

Wide table:

- Columns: `Name`, (Run, no visible header; aria `Run`), `Runs`, `Last run` (with a down chevron, sorted newest first), `Next run`, `Created`, (menu, no header)
- aria for the table: `Routines`
- Run button: `Run`, or `Stop` while running. aria: `Run <name> now`, or `Stop <name>`
- Runs: the count, `<n>`
- Last run: `Today <time>`, `Yesterday <time>`, else `<Weekday>, <Mon> <day>` (for example `Fri, Nov 6`). A run that didn't start: `Didn't start` (its time is the tooltip). While running: `Running · <elapsed>` (elapsed `0:42`, `12:05`, `1:02:09`)
- Next run: `In <n> minute(s)`, `In <n> hour(s)`, `In <n> day(s)`, or `Off`, `Done`, `None` (no schedule)
- Created: `now`, `<n>m`, `<n>h`, `<n>d`

Narrow table (beside an open editor, and on a phone):

- Columns: `Routine`, `Runs`, `Last run`, (menu). The Run button sits right after the name, on its first line (no Run column). On a phone (760 px or narrower) there is no `Runs` column (it is in the editor), and a long name takes up to two lines.

- Heading: `Off` with its count `<n>`

Row menu:

- Trigger aria: `More for <name>`. Popup aria: `<name>`
- Items: `Turn off` or `Turn on` (absent once Done), `Delete`

## 5. The editor

Source: `scheduled/ScheduledEditor.tsx`, `scheduled/ScheduleRow.tsx`, `scheduled/EditorParts.tsx`, `scheduled/words.ts`, `packages/core/inbox-scheduled.ts`.

Header:

- Back (narrow): `Routines`. aria: `Back to routines`
- More menu: aria `More`, popup aria `Routine`. Items: `Turn off` or `Turn on` (absent once Done), `Delete`
- Close: tooltip and aria `Close`

Name and meta line:

- Name field placeholder and aria: `Name`
- Switch and its word: `On` or `Off`. Once Done, in place of the switch: `Done · ran <time>` (`<time>` as in Runs below, without `Today`), `Done · didn't start`, or `Done · didn't run` (its one time was skipped)
- `Replies in <thread name>` (the thread name is a link; shown once it has a thread)
- `Runs on this computer while the Inbox is running`

Schedule group:

- Heading: `Schedule`
- Kind picker, as shown: `Every hour`, `Every day`, `Every weekday`, `Every week`, `Once`, `Custom`, `No schedule`. aria: `Schedule: <shown>. Change`
- Kind menu items: `Hourly`, `Daily`, `Weekdays`, `Weekly`, `Once`, `Custom`, then a rule, then `No schedule`
- Hourly: `at` and a minute menu `:00` to `:55` (aria `Minute`)
- Weekly: `on` and a day menu `Sunday` to `Saturday` (aria `Day`)
- Once: `on` and a date field (aria `Date`)
- Daily, Weekdays, Weekly, Once: `at` and a time field (aria `Time`)
- Custom: a cron field (aria `Cron`). Under the row, when it is accepted: the schedule words, for example `Every weekday at 9:00 AM`, `Every 2 hours, at minute 0`, `Every Monday and Wednesday at 9:00 AM`, `Every month on day 1 at 9:00 AM`, `Every 20 minutes`, `Every hour at :00 and :45` (a minute step that does not divide the hour says its minutes), `On the schedule <cron>` (any other pattern, an hour step that does not divide the day among them)

- Time zone: the zone's short name (`EST`), or the zone id before the preview answers. aria: `Time zone`
- Next run line: `Next run <Wkd>, <Mon> <day> at <time> <zone>` (for example `Next run Mon, Nov 16 at 9:00 AM EST`)
- Refusals, under the row in place of the next run:
  - `Scheduled times are at least 15 minutes apart. This one runs every <n> minutes.`

  - `That isn't a schedule: <YYYY-MM-DD> at <HH:MM> is not a real date and time.`

Prompt group:

- Heading: `Prompt`

- Foot: `Runs as` then the agent's name (`Claude Code`, `Codex`, `OpenCode`, `Pi`). aria: `Agent: <name>. Change`. Menu aria: `Agent`. The model and effort button is New message's own.

Repo or folder, and Files (group aria `What it works with`):

- `Repo or folder` (the label; it was `Folder`): a chip with `~/<path>`, `New scratch folder`, `A folder that is gone`, or `Pick a folder`. The menu is New message's folder menu.
- `Files`: one chip per file with its file name (tooltip: the full path). Remove aria: `Remove <file name>`
- `Add file`, then a path field: placeholder `/path/to/file`, aria `File path`

Runs (once it has run):

- Heading: `Runs` with its count `<n>`
- Each row, newest first, at most 5: `Run <n>`, then `Running`, `Replied`, `Didn't finish` or `Didn't start`, then `Today <time>`, `<Wkd> <time>` within the week, else `<Mon> <day>, <time>`
- More than 5: `All <n> in the thread`

Errors: one error line with the server's message (section 9).

Footer button: `Run now` (disabled until it is made), or `Stop` while running.

## 6. The thread

Source: `scheduled/RunDivider.tsx`, `scheduled/words.ts`, `scheduled/ScheduledFoot.tsx`, `scheduled/farLinks.ts`, `components/Thread.tsx`.

Thread header, under the title (a thread whose first message is a scheduled run; an ordinary launched thread keeps `You started <agent> in <project>`):

- `Routine · <agent name> in <project>`

Run divider:

- Late: `Run <n> · due <when>, ran <time>` (`<when>` is `9:00 AM` on the same day, `yesterday 9:00 AM`, `Wed 2:00 AM` within the week, else `Nov 2, 9:00 AM`)

Skip line:

- `Skipped <when> · <reason>`, or `Skipped <n> times, <when> to <when> · <reason>`

A reason this window does not know (a newer Inbox's): `Skipped <when>` alone. With no skip details at all: `Skipped`.

Under a run:

## 7. The Inbox list row

Source: `scheduled/rowLook.tsx`, `components/RowSlot.tsx`, `components/InboxList.tsx`.

## 8. Toasts

issues.title: Inbox agent text: the owner's lessons for agents

labels.name: ci:e2e
labels.description: Run the full browser suite (Inbox window e2e) on this PR

issues.body:
Adds the eleven sentences the owner approved word for word (2026-11-15) to the text agents read. No other agent-facing words change, and no length budget moves.

**Where each one went**
1. Prototype ("Open it and click through…"): in the option lines on send_message's `body` (agent tool, MCP field), and in `--help`'s `Prototype:` line.
2–4. Their own idea in their words, a part of the screen as the person sees it, numbered pictures or a video: one paragraph right before the pictures rule on every `body` copy, in `--help` and in llms.txt. The "no jargon" sentence exists only in Bro mode, so these sit in the body itself.
5. "An answer that asks something back…": a paragraph in the wake when a reply carries "Answers to your questions" (never a New message), and in `--help` and llms.txt. It is not in the MCP server instructions: they would reach 2,142 characters.
6. Real screenshot: the end of the pictures rule, so every `body` copy, `--help` and llms.txt.
7. "Search before you say…": the MCP search description and `--help`. It is **not** on the agent tool's search line: with steps on, the description would reach 2,086 characters (the cap is 2,048).
8. New big issue, new thread: the end of every `thread` field (agent tool, MCP send_message and submit_guide), `--help`, llms.txt.
9. Reread: the last line of every `body` copy, plus `--help` and llms.txt.
10. "Ask only about things the person would recognise…": right after "Ask only what you cannot decide alone" on the agent tool's `body`, and after the question guide in `--help` and llms.txt. It is **not** in the shared question guide: that guide is send_message's MCP description, and Claude Code's cut would then drop its `- [x]` rule (inbox.test.ts pins it). So the skill does not carry it.
11. "Take it as a go.": only at the end of the 👍 Looks good line, not on any other reaction or on a 👍 the person renamed.

**Size** (Pi/OpenCode send the tool with every request): the description stays 1,944 characters. The whole entry goes from 13,084 to 13,869 bytes (+785, about +212 tokens). `INBOX_TOOL_COST` and the docs' stated figures are updated to the measured numbers (they have a 5% drift test).

**Tests**: `tests/inbox-agent-text-lessons.test.ts` checks that each sentence is on each host's copy and that only 👍 Looks good gets "go". The tests that pinned the old 👍 line are updated.

**Clean room** (fresh Sonnet agents with only the tool text and wake, 3 runs each, with vs without): an "Other: hmm, what about retrying twice?" answer was read back and waited on 3/3 vs 0/3. A second big issue mid-thread got its own thread and a pointer in the old one 3/3 vs 0/3 (all six opened the new thread). A 👍 on a proposal started the work 3/3 vs 3/3. With one product decision and two implementation details, 0/6 vs 0/6 asked only the product one: every agent asked all three.

issues.title: Inbox tags step 2: header tag line, Tag filter, tags in Search, Board-off preview

labels.name: ci:e2e
labels.description: Run the full browser suite (Inbox window e2e) on this PR

issues.body:
Step 2 of Inbox thread tags: the parts of the approved design that were not built in step 1. A thread's tags now show under its subject, the list's Filter and Search can each narrow to tags, and with the Board off a sent `#Tag` previews its threads.

## What changes for the person

- **The header line.** Under a thread's subject: one `#`, the thread's tags as plain names (each opens the tag's list), then `+` (Add tag). `+` opens the same tick list as the row menu. A thread with no tags shows nothing, so most threads look as they do today. An archived thread (open from the Archived group, Search or Settings) shows its tags too: the thread read's `row` now carries `tags`, as the list's rows do. On a phone the tags are 32 px tall and `+` opens a bottom sheet.
- **Filter.** The list's Filter has a Tag group: each name with a `#` in the icon column (as the mock had), how many threads each leaves, and a tick. Picking several tags shows threads in any of them. Until the list is read, the picks hold, so the rows never show unfiltered for a moment. Tags combine with Not seen, Updated, Agent, Pull request and Project as those groups already combine. Like the list's other filters, the Tag filter applies to the Archived group's rows too (#3404). The group shows only while a tag holds a listed thread. On a tag's own list the Tag picks step aside, as Project picks do on a project's page.
- **Search.** Tags are never search results: the results for any words are the same as on main. Search gets a Tag chip after "From anyone", in the same style: "Any tag", or pick one or more of the tags this Inbox's own threads carry (search reads only those, as on main; the menu stays open for more ticks). Several tags are either/or ("Tagged Release or Windows"); the chip is "and" with the other chips; its × clears it; "Searched only Tagged Release." names it under the results. The chip shows once there is such a tag. `#rel` is plain text again. The server takes `tag=ini_…` (repeatable, at most 200, a repeated id counted once); the window sends one id per picked tag.
- **Header `+` by keyboard.** Enter, Space or Down on `+` open the list as a click does, with focus in the field (before, focus went to the first tag and typed letters went to the menu).
- **Board-off preview.** With the Board off, resting on a sent `#Windows` (or focusing it, or a first tap on a phone) shows the tag's name, "Tag · projects · N threads", its latest threads (not the one you are reading), and "Show threads". With the Board on, the Board's preview is unchanged.

## Linked machines

Everything reads the window's merged tags and rows. A linked machine's threads count in the Filter and show in the preview, and its thread's header line shows and edits its tags through the link, as Add tag does since #3330. An older machine that keeps no tags shows no line, and its rows are in no tag. Search covers this Inbox's own threads only, as on main, so its Tag chip offers only the tags those threads carry: a tag only a linked machine's threads carry is not offered (it could only find nothing).

## For agents

Nothing changes. Agents do not read thread tags, and this adds no agent-facing text.

## Decided here, for the owner to confirm

- The header line uses `#` once with plain names (the record's "`#` once").
- The Tag group sits after Pull request and before Project.
- The header `+` list has no Back row; on a phone its sheet is titled "Add tag".
- Header tag names have no hover preview; they are links.
- Search's Tag chip sits last, after From; "Any tag" clears and closes the menu, a tag tick keeps it open; tags are matched by thread, so a tag filter hides project results.

New words on screen: "Tag" (Filter heading, Search's Tag menu label), "Tags" (the header list's label), "Any tag", "Tagged {name}", "Tagged {a} or {b}", "Clear the tag filter" (the chip's × label), "Tag · {projects} · {n} threads", "Show threads", "+{n} more", "Add tag" (the `+` button's tooltip and the phone sheet's title).

## Tests

- `packages/inbox/threadTagsStep2.test.tsx` (new, DOM): the header line shows and edits tags, including a linked machine's thread written by name and an older machine's showing none; the Filter's Tag group with one and several tags combined with Agent; Search results with tags equal those without for `#rel`, `rel` and `move`; the Tag chip picks several, sends every machine's id, combines with From, clears with ×, and is absent with no tags; the header `+` opened by keyboard with focus in the field, which keeps it while typing moves the rows (#3393); a tag only a linked machine carries is not offered in Search; the Board-off preview by hover and by tap, including a tag only the linked machine holds; nothing new with zero tags.

issues.title: Inbox: name unattached PRs (bare #N too) in send_message's result

labels.name: ci:e2e
labels.description: Run the full browser suite (Inbox window e2e) on this PR

issues.body:
Agents name their PRs in Inbox messages but rarely put them on the thread's row. With this change, send_message's result names each PR the message mentions that is on no thread's row, one line per PR and at most three, in the owner's words:

`You named #3405, which is on no thread's row. If it is this work's PR, attach it: thread_pulls with add ["owner/repo#3405"].`

- **What counts on the send.** A bare `#3405` (read against the thread's project repository, from the cached `origin`) or `owner/repo#3405` counts when the Inbox already knows the number is a PR:
  - the Pull requests list holds it;
  - a hover card already read it;
  - a PR URL for it appears in any message of the project, the agent's or the person's (`storePullKeys`, read with the Pull requests page's `inboxPullUrlsIn`);
  - it is on, or was taken off, any thread's row;
  - an earlier lookup found it.

  URLs and GitLab `group/project!45` count as before.
- **The lookup after the send** (the owner's call: "look it up after the message is sent"; `packages/server/inbox-pull-lookups.ts`):
  - When to look: a number in the project's GitHub repository that the Inbox knows neither as a PR nor as an issue is looked up once, after the send has answered. Nothing runs on the send path, and a failure is silent.
  - How: through the hover cards' read (`refCards.get`, one `issueOrPullRequest` query, the same hosts, accounts, rate-limit pause and CLI slots). It runs only while Code review is on and this computer's gh is signed in to the host; otherwise nothing runs.
  - Limits: at most 3 numbers per message, one read at a time, 30 waiting.
  - Cache: the answers (`pull` / `issue` / `missing`) are kept in memory, at most 5,000, least recently used dropped first. A restart forgets them. An offline or signed-out read keeps nothing.
  - The line: a PR found this way is named on that agent's next send in the thread.
  - Scope: GitHub only, because on GitLab a `#12` is an issue.
- **When it stays quiet.**
  - A PR is named once per thread. Another thread that names it still hears it.
  - There is no line when the PR is on any thread's row, or is passed in the same call's `pulls` (even when that add was refused).
  - A PR taken off this thread is never named there again.
  - An issue is never named. Nothing is auto-attached.
  - A send with no `agent_session` now gets the PR line too (it used to get none). The question-options line still needs a session.
- **Bounded on any body.** A body is read for at most 50 distinct refs of each form. The lookup's pick stops at 3. A number past GitHub's 32 bits is never named or looked up. A body naming 50,000 numbers is a test: the send's lines and the pick each take under 200 ms, and 3 are queued.

There are no wording changes, so nothing is added to any text under Claude Code's 2,048-character cut.

Tests:
- `packages/server/inbox-mcp-hints.test.ts`:
  - the line itself, once per thread, the cap of three, the quiet cases (rows, `pulls`, removed from this thread);
  - the store's links (agent's and person's) and removals;
  - with a lookup: no line on the first send, the lookup after it, the line on that agent's next send; an issue never; Code review off or a failing forge, nothing; a message with 40 numbers asks about 3.
- `packages/server/inbox-pull-lookups.test.ts`:
  - kept answers are never asked again;
  - per-message cap, one read at a time, a bounded wait;
  - failures and an unusable forge keep nothing;
  - the card read on a stand-in gh: PR, issue, missing, offline, signed out.

Clean-room check: fresh agents had only main's tool text. The results came from the real send_message handlers on a temporary store, with no PR page open and a stand-in forge. The task: a subagent's report names bare `#3405` (a PR) and `#3399` (an issue), the agent cannot learn the repository, and it posts twice in one thread.

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Attached the PR | 0 of 3 | 3 of 3, with `thread_pulls` add `["acme/api#3405"]` after the line on the second send |
| Line on the first send | none | none |
| Attached the issue | none | none |

issues.title: Inbox: a T3 Code group in Settings → Agents
issues.body:
## What this does

Settings → Agents gets a T3 Code group, right after Codex. It shows only when T3 Code is on this computer. It has one row, Your replies:

- T3's own `t3` command is here and T3 is open: "arrive as a new turn", Connected.
- The same, but T3 is closed now: the same, plus "T3 isn't open. They go in when you open it."
- Nothing here can wake a T3 thread (Windows, or no `t3` command, and no saved sign-in that can send): "seen when it checks the Inbox; it can't be woken", Not connected, and under it the sign-in sentence from the T3 waiting line with `plannotator t3 login --url <T3 MCP URL>` and Copy. Hovering the command says where the URL is in T3.

A saved sign-in that can send counts as Connected too. The Agents item in Settings gets no dot from this group.

## Server

`GET /api/inbox/agents` now carries `t3: { local, open, sign_in }`, or null when T3 is not on this computer. It is read on every agents read with no process run: T3's home folder, its launcher or a `t3` on PATH (Windows included), whether its runtime file names a live process, and the saved sign-ins (`none`, `ok`, `read_only`, `ran_out` once T3 refused one). It never carries a token or a URL. An older Inbox leaves the field out, so the window shows no group. Settings → Agents is per machine, so a linked machine shows its own T3 state only on its own Settings page.

## Icon

The group uses the neutral code glyph, as T3 threads do elsewhere: the icon set has no T3 Code logo yet. The mark comes from one constant (`T3_CODE_MARK_HOST`), so adding a `t3` mark to the shared icon set changes it here and on T3 threads together.

## Tests

- `packages/inbox/t3AgentGroup.test.tsx` (DOM): no group when T3 is not found; the words of each state; the fix line and Copy only when nothing can wake it; no dot on the Agents item (and a session that needs a reload still lights it).
- `packages/server/inbox-t3-settings.test.ts`: not found, open and closed, found with no command and on Windows, and the saved sign-ins including one T3 refused; no token or URL in the answer.
